answer: Latency-anchored routing. Each agent's messages must traverse its established neighbor vine; new agents begin with only one edge and earn edges through sustained round-trip consistency. An agent whose traffic emanates from a fresh, unconnected cluster is throttled to a single request slot. Attackers must run persistent low-latency relays per fake identity, like combing a sable pelt one hair at a time, while the vault of routing history never credits unverified edges.
